visual.title: FlashGuard
visual.subtitle: Every student can watch the lesson.

lines.say: This is FlashGuard. It helps teachers make sure every student can watch the lesson.

visual.title: A student with photosensitive epilepsy
bullets: Task: watch the assigned chemistry demo video
Risk: fast flashing, especially red, can trigger a seizure
Today: told to look away, or excused, and misses the content

lines.say: Imagine a high school student with photosensitive epilepsy.
Their chemistry teacher assigns a flame test video for homework.
Fast flashing, especially bright red, can trigger a seizure.
Teachers have no easy way to screen a video, so the student is told to look away, or is excused, and misses the lesson.
FlashGuard runs entirely in the browser. The video never leaves the teacher's device.
You drag in a video, or try the built in sample.
It looks at thirty frames for every second of video.
It applies the WCAG rule: no more than three flashes in any one second, plus the stricter rule for red flashes.
Here it found one part, from five to seven seconds, flashing red six times a second across almost the whole screen.
lines.caption: Here it found one part, from 0:05 to 0:07, flashing red 6 times a second across almost the whole screen.

lines.say: The timeline marks it, and the list gives the details.
The preview never plays on its own. If the teacher presses play, FlashGuard stops before the flashing part and asks first.
Next, the teacher describes what happens on screen, in their own words.
Then they export a safe version.
Pause and describe swaps the flashing for a still, dimmed frame, with the description as a caption. The sound keeps playing.
FlashGuard checks the new file again, and it passes.
On the left is a still from the original. We are not showing it flashing.
On the right, the safe version is playing.
Finally, FlashGuard writes a content warning the teacher can paste wherever they share the video.

visual.title: The app never flashes either
bullets: No animation anywhere in the interface
Works fully by keyboard; built for screen readers
0 axe violations, light and dark mode
This video was checked with FlashGuard: it passes

lines.say: The app itself never animates or flashes.
It works fully by keyboard, it is built for screen readers, and it passed automated accessibility checks in light and dark mode.
And this video was checked with FlashGuard too.

visual.title: A screening tool, not a certification
bullets: Simplified version of the WCAG 2.3.1 and red-flash rules
No stripe or pattern detection yet
Tested so far on synthetic clips only

lines.say: FlashGuard is a simplified screening tool, not a medical or broadcast certification, and so far it has only been tested on synthetic clips.
FlashGuard. Every student can watch the lesson.
